t: Corporate Flight Bookings — Difference Array Editorial
o: We must compute, for each of n flights, the total seats reserved across all bookings whose range covers that flight. A naive reading suggests: for each booking [first, last, seats], add seats to every flight in the range. In Example 1, booking [1,2,10] adds 10 to flights 1–2, [2,3,20] adds 20 to flights 2–3, and [2,5,25] adds 25 to flights 2–5, giving totals [10,55,45,25,25]. With n and bookings both up to 2·10^4, brute force costs up to ~4·10^8 range updates — too slow in the worst case. The key observation is that we only need final totals, not intermediate states, which points to a difference array: record range updates in O(1) each, then one prefix-sum pass recovers all answers.
k: Each booking is a constant-addition over a contiguous range; only final per-flight sums are needed.
A difference array turns any range update into two O(1) point updates.
One left-to-right prefix sum pass converts differences back into actual seat counts.

a.i: Directly simulate the problem statement: for every booking, loop over its flight range and add seats to each flight. This is exactly what the examples describe and is trivially correct. It works within constraints for small inputs but degrades when many bookings cover long ranges.
s: Initialize an answer array of length n with zeros.
For each booking [first, last, seats], iterate i from first-1 to last-1 (0-indexed).
Add seats to answer[i] for each i in that range.
a.t: O(m · n) worst case — each of m bookings may update up to n flights.
a.sp: O(1) extra space beyond the output array.

a.i: Instead of adding seats across a whole range, mark only the boundaries. For booking [first, last, seats], add seats at index first-1 and subtract seats just after index last-1. Then a single running sum from left to right accumulates exactly the correct total at every flight: each subtraction cancels the effect once the range ends. This reduces each update to O(1), so total work is O(n + m).
s: Create diff array of length n+1 initialized to zero.
For each booking [first, last, seats]: diff[first-1] += seats; diff[last] -= seats.
Run a running total over diff[0..n-1], writing it into answer[i].
a.t: O(n + m) — O(1) per booking plus one linear prefix-sum pass.
a.sp: O(n) for the difference array (can be done in-place on the output for O(1) extra).

w: In an interview, mention the brute force briefly, then lead with the difference array — it's the expected solution and generalizes to any 'range add, point query' problem. Pitfalls: off-by-one errors converting 1-indexed flights to 0-indexed arrays (add at first-1, subtract at last); forgetting the extra slot so diff[last] doesn't overflow; and integer overflow in languages like C++/Java if values were larger (here max total is 2·10^4 · 10^4 = 2·10^8, which fits in int, but be ready to justify it). Edge cases: single-flight bookings (first == last) and bookings covering the entire range. Follow-ups: support mixed range-add/range-query operations (use a Fenwick/BIT or segment tree), or handle streaming bookings where you must answer queries online.
